correctness.rationale: Every inclusion-maximal abelian subalgebra contains the central edge space Z=F_q^E, so it corresponds to a maximal commuting linear vertex subspace U. The alternating bracket coefficient at each graph edge {i,j} is λ_i∧λ_j, requiring nonzero restricted coordinate functionals to be proportional along each connected component C of active support S. U therefore lies in W_S spanned by one all-nonzero-supported generator for each induced component, and maximality forces equality. An outside vertex with no S neighbor extends W_S, while domination forces the full centralizer in vertex space to equal W_S, proving maximality iff S dominates. The projective-line choices per component give (q-1)^{|S|-c(G[S])}; dimensions |E|+c, and max degree α(G) follows because representatives of components form independent sets and every maximum independent set dominates. Works for char 2, isolates and disconnected graphs. Independently enumerated all RREF vertex subspaces and literal centralizers for every graph on 1..3 labeled vertices over F_2,F_3 (22 graph-field cases), comparing against a separately coded dominating-set/component census. The asserted unrestricted formula rests on functional proportionality, not finite enumeration.

originality.rationale: The completed statement classifies and counts every embedded inclusion-maximal abelian subalgebra over any F_q in the independent-central-edge graph construction. Projective noncommuting-graph maximal independent sets are an equivalent abstract formulation (Sriwongsa Prop. 2.8), but they do not evaluate the graph-induced weighted domination polynomial. Aldi et al. define a Lie independence polynomial and prove upper dimension bounds, which are not this polynomial or its coefficients. DeCoste et al. analyze an abelian central direct-summand factor, not all embedded maximal commuting subspaces. The finite-field enumeration was compared with those mathematical objects rather than only shared graph/Lie vocabulary.
residual_risks: Projective noncommuting-graph independence enumerations might encode the same numbers in a different graph-polynomial formalism; an unindexed explicit specialization cannot be ruled out.
Independent small-field computation verifies examples but not the all-q result without the proved component-functional lemma.

value.rationale: A complete natural classification and coefficient-wise enumerator of maximal (not merely maximum-size) commuting subalgebras is a substantive missing invariant for graph two-step Lie algebras; it both refines the independence number and can distinguish graphs sharing an independence polynomial (the paw versus C4 example). The graph-domination weights and q parameter encode embedded multiplicity rather than rebranding existing independent-set counts; the result includes all finite graphs, characteristics and component structures.
